variants.title: Run the governance loop
variants.context: The governance loop runs from system inventory to risk and role map to control evidence to decision record to the operations loop. The decision record points back to the exact system and forward to monitoring, incidents, and recertification.
variants.prompt: A new AI system is being brought under governance for the first time. Put the loop in order.

items.text: Write the decision record: approver, scope, residual risk, conditions, expiry, and rollback criteria.
Close the operations loop: join production signals and incidents to that decision and reassess material changes.
Collect control evidence: bind tests, reviews, oversight drills, and mitigations to immutable component versions.
Build the system inventory entry: purpose, owners, users, regions, models, data, tools, providers, and prohibited uses.
Map risk and role: plausible harms, affected groups, autonomy, reversibility, and the organization's role.

variants.hint: Which step tells you which harms are even plausible?
variants.explanation: Traceable accountability means every material decision connects a system version and risk to an owner, evidence, control, decision, and follow-up.

variants.title: Run the governance loop
variants.context: The governance loop runs from system inventory to risk and role map to control evidence to decision record to the operations loop. The decision record points back to the exact system and forward to monitoring, incidents, and recertification.
variants.prompt: A reviewer asks how a deployed assistant earned its current level of exposure. Put the artifacts in the order that answers the question.

items.text: The risk and role map states who can be harmed, how reversible the harm is, and whether the organization is a provider or a deployer.
The operations record shows the production signals and incidents that have been joined back to that decision.
The decision record shows who approved which scope, with what residual risk, expiry, and rollback criteria.
The control evidence shows which tests and oversight drills ran against those exact component versions.
The inventory entry names what this system is for, who runs it, and which regions and providers it touches.

variants.hint: The chain has to be walkable from purpose all the way to production.
variants.explanation: The useful question is not whether documents exist, but whether a reviewer can reconstruct why this exact system received this exact exposure.

variants.title: Run the governance loop
variants.context: The governance loop runs from system inventory to risk and role map to control evidence to decision record to the operations loop. The decision record points back to the exact system and forward to monitoring, incidents, and recertification.
variants.prompt: A provider swap moves the system to a new region and a new user population. Put the loop in order as it reopens.

items.text: Re-map the plausible harms, affected groups, and the organization's role for that population.
Issue a new decision record with approver, scope, residual risk, conditions, expiry, and rollback criteria.
Update the inventory with the new provider, region, and user population.
Re-bind control evidence to the new immutable component versions rather than reusing the old attachments.
Rejoin production signals and incidents to the new decision so the next material change is caught.

variants.hint: A material change restarts the loop rather than appending to the old record.
variants.explanation: Decisions and evidence expire deliberately, so an old approval never authorizes an unbounded future system.

variants.title: Reassess a material change
variants.context: Governance is change impact analysis. Describe the delta, trace it to the claims it invalidates, re-run the smallest sufficient evidence set, then approve only the exposure that evidence supports, with an expiry and stop conditions.
variants.prompt: A release changes the system prompt in a way that affects refusal behavior. Put the reassessment in order.

items.text: Refresh evidence: re-run the smallest sufficient set while preserving independent review for high-consequence claims.
Bound the decision: approve only the exposure the refreshed evidence supports, with an expiry and concrete stop conditions.
Describe the delta: diff model, prompt, policy, data, tools, user population, regions, autonomy, and human oversight.
Find the invalidated claims: trace the changed prompt to the evaluations, risk claims, documentation, and operational controls that depend on it.

variants.hint: Which evidence actually depended on the thing that changed?
variants.explanation: Change impact analysis reruns the smallest sufficient set, which is neither reusing everything nor rerunning every control indiscriminately.

variants.title: Reassess a material change
variants.context: Governance is change impact analysis. Describe the delta, trace it to the claims it invalidates, re-run the smallest sufficient evidence set, then approve only the exposure that evidence supports, with an expiry and stop conditions.
variants.prompt: A dependency upgrade touches no model, prompt, policy, data, or tool behavior. Put the reassessment in order.

items.text: Re-run only the controls that the diff touches, leaving the independent reviews in force.
Reuse the current decision within its existing scope and expiry rather than opening a new approval.
Diff every governed component and confirm that none of the behavior-bearing ones moved.
Trace the changed component and find that no risk claim or evaluation depended on it.

variants.hint: A patch and a purpose change do not deserve the same review.
variants.explanation: Controls are proportionate: a low-risk change that invalidates no claim can reuse current evidence inside its declared scope and expiry.

variants.title: Reassess a material change
variants.context: Governance is change impact analysis. Describe the delta, trace it to the claims it invalidates, re-run the smallest sufficient evidence set, then approve only the exposure that evidence supports, with an expiry and stop conditions.
variants.prompt: The same assistant is being extended from internal staff to members of the public. Put the reassessment in order.

items.text: Trace it to the risk map, the affected-groups analysis, the oversight design, and every claim scoped to internal users.
Approve only the bounded public exposure the new evidence supports, with an expiry and stop conditions.
Re-run risk mapping and the evaluations that were scoped to the old population, keeping independent review for the high-consequence claims.
Describe the delta as a change of user population, region, and effective autonomy, not only a configuration edit.

variants.hint: A population change reopens more than the evaluation numbers.
variants.explanation: A model, purpose, or population change can reopen risk mapping and independent review, because the claims themselves were scoped to the old context.

variants.title: Fail closed on the evidence
variants.context: A release packet is reproducible only when artifacts agree on identity. Evidence has to name what was assessed, whether it is still usable, and what decision it supports, and the ledger fails closed when it is missing, failed, expired, or attached to the wrong version.
variants.prompt: The safety evaluation was run against retrieval corpus snapshot 2026-06, but the deployment now serves snapshot 2026-09. What should the gate conclude?
options: The evidence is attached to the wrong subject version, so the corpus-dependent claims must be refreshed.
The evidence still holds, because the model, prompt, and policy versions are all unchanged.
The evidence holds if the newer corpus is a superset of the one that was assessed.
optionFeedback: Correct: the corpus is a pinned component of identity, so evidence bound to the old snapshot cannot authorize the new one.
The corpus is part of what was assessed, so leaving the model unchanged does not preserve the claim.
Adding documents changes retrieved context and therefore the behavior the evaluation measured.
variants.hint: Which components does the packet claim to have assessed?
variants.explanation: Identity pins model, prompt, policy, tools, retrieval corpus, dataset, evaluator, and application versions; evidence bound to one version cannot authorize another.

variants.title: Fail closed on the evidence
variants.context: A release packet is reproducible only when artifacts agree on identity. Evidence has to name what was assessed, whether it is still usable, and what decision it supports, and the ledger fails closed when it is missing, failed, expired, or attached to the wrong version.
variants.prompt: Every artifact in the packet passed, but the independent bias review expired two months ago and nothing about the system changed. What should the gate conclude?
options: An unchanged system keeps its evidence valid, since expiry only matters after a change.
The gate can proceed and record the expiry as an accepted exception without a renewal.
Expired evidence fails closed, so the review is renewed before the decision proceeds.
optionFeedback: Expiry exists precisely so that an old approval cannot authorize an unbounded future system.
Recording an exception is not the same as having current evidence for a high-consequence claim.
Correct: the ledger fails closed on missing, failed, or expired evidence regardless of whether the system moved.
variants.hint: What is an expiry date for, if not this situation?
variants.explanation: Validity is a property of the evidence itself: outcome, scope, owner, provenance, completion time, expiry, and review status all have to be current.

variants.title: Fail closed on the evidence
variants.context: A release packet is reproducible only when artifacts agree on identity. Evidence has to name what was assessed, whether it is still usable, and what decision it supports, and the ledger fails closed when it is missing, failed, expired, or attached to the wrong version.
variants.prompt: The evaluation was scoped to an internal pilot of 200 staff, and the team now requests general public availability. What should the gate conclude?
options: Approve only the exposure the current evidence scope supports, and re-scope before going further.
Approve the public launch, because the evaluation passed every declared threshold.
Approve the public launch with monitoring, treating production traffic as the missing evidence.
optionFeedback: Correct: the decision binds evidence to an exposure limit, so a claim scoped to a pilot cannot authorize general availability.
Passing thresholds inside a scope says nothing about the population the scope excluded.
Monitoring is governance evidence only when a signal has an owner and a decision threshold, not as a substitute for scoped evaluation.
variants.hint: What population did the evidence actually cover?
variants.explanation: The decision binds evidence to approval conditions, residual risk, an exposure limit, a rollback trigger, and a next review, so exposure never exceeds scope.

variants.title: Use the RMF functions
variants.context: The NIST AI RMF organizes work into four functions. Govern is cross-cutting, Map supplies context, Measure produces evidence with uncertainty and slices, and Manage prioritizes, treats, monitors, and recovers. They are outcomes, not a strict sequence.
variants.prompt: Match each NIST AI RMF function to the work it names.

pairs.label: Govern
pairs.detail: Risk tolerance, roles, escalation paths, inventory rules, review cadence, and retirement responsibilities.

pairs.label: Map
pairs.detail: Intended use, affected people, dependencies, foreseeable misuse, impacts, and assumptions.

pairs.label: Measure
pairs.detail: Evaluation of risks and controls with quantitative and qualitative methods, uncertainty, slices, and independent review.

pairs.label: Manage
pairs.detail: Prioritizing risks, choosing treatment, constraining or stopping deployment, monitoring, recovering, and communicating.

variants.hint: One of these four is cross-cutting rather than a stage.
variants.explanation: Govern is cross-cutting while Map informs Measure and Measure informs Manage, so the functions are connected outcomes rather than a checklist.

variants.title: Use the RMF functions
variants.context: The NIST AI RMF organizes work into four functions. Govern is cross-cutting, Map supplies context, Measure produces evidence with uncertainty and slices, and Manage prioritizes, treats, monitors, and recovers. They are outcomes, not a strict sequence.
variants.prompt: Match each activity to the function it belongs to.

pairs.label: Writing down who may approve a launch and when approvals expire
pairs.detail: Govern, which owns roles, escalation, and review cadence.

pairs.label: Listing the groups who could be harmed if the assistant refuses wrongly
pairs.detail: Map, which supplies the context the evidence is later judged against.

pairs.label: Reporting slice results with denominators and an independent reviewer's sign-off
pairs.detail: Measure, which produces evidence with uncertainty and review.

pairs.label: Cutting exposure and triggering a rollback after a production signal crosses its threshold
pairs.detail: Manage, which treats risk and recovers.

variants.hint: Ask whether the activity sets the rules, supplies context, produces evidence, or takes action.
variants.explanation: The practical output is a profile for this use case, so each activity has to land in the function that actually owns it.

variants.title: Use the RMF functions
variants.context: The NIST AI RMF organizes work into four functions. Govern is cross-cutting, Map supplies context, Measure produces evidence with uncertainty and slices, and Manage prioritizes, treats, monitors, and recovers. They are outcomes, not a strict sequence.
variants.prompt: Match each reviewer question to the function that answers it.

pairs.label: Who is allowed to accept this residual risk, and by when must the decision be revisited?
pairs.detail: Govern.

pairs.label: Which people are affected, and what does foreseeable misuse look like?
pairs.detail: Map.

pairs.label: How certain are we, and which slices were tested by whom?
pairs.detail: Measure.

pairs.label: What are we doing about it, and how do we stop if it goes wrong?
pairs.detail: Manage.

variants.hint: Each question names a different kind of answer: authority, context, evidence, or action.
variants.explanation: Controls should be proportionate to context and documented risk tolerance, which is why the four questions stay separate rather than collapsing into one review.

variants.title: Give the decision an owner
variants.context: Every material decision has a named owner. Engineering builds and operates the controls, risk and legal interpret obligations and challenge assumptions, and the business owner accepts the residual risk. Independence rises with potential harm, uncertainty, and irreversibility.
variants.prompt: Match each function to what it is accountable for.

pairs.label: Engineering
pairs.detail: Versioning, evidence capture, release gates, monitoring, access controls, rollback, and retention boundaries.

pairs.label: Risk and legal
pairs.detail: Interpreting obligations, defining risk tolerance, challenging assumptions, and advising on notifications and prohibited uses.

pairs.label: Business owner
pairs.detail: The intended use, benefits, affected users, operating conditions, residual risk, and the decision to proceed or stop.

variants.hint: Ask who builds it, who interprets it, and who accepts the consequences.
variants.explanation: Accountability is only traceable when each material decision has a named owner rather than a committee that produced and approved its own claim.

variants.title: Give the decision an owner
variants.context: Every material decision has a named owner. Engineering builds and operates the controls, risk and legal interpret obligations and challenge assumptions, and the business owner accepts the residual risk. Independence rises with potential harm, uncertainty, and irreversibility.
variants.prompt: Match each pending decision to the function that owns it.

pairs.label: Whether the residual risk is acceptable and the launch proceeds
pairs.detail: The business owner, who accepts accountability for the intended use.

pairs.label: Whether the rollback path and retention boundary actually work
pairs.detail: Engineering, which builds and operates those controls.

pairs.label: Which jurisdiction and organizational role the obligations snapshot should record
pairs.detail: Risk and legal, which interprets obligations and names the interpretation owner.

pairs.label: Whether this claim needs an independent reviewer at all
pairs.detail: Risk and legal with the business owner, since independence scales with harm and irreversibility.

variants.hint: Follow the accountability, not the calendar or who is available.
variants.explanation: Storing an obligations snapshot with a named legal interpretation owner is what keeps a regulatory reading auditable later.

variants.title: Give the decision an owner
variants.context: Every material decision has a named owner. Engineering builds and operates the controls, risk and legal interpret obligations and challenge assumptions, and the business owner accepts the residual risk. Independence rises with potential harm, uncertainty, and irreversibility.
variants.prompt: Match each observed practice to the accountability rule it breaks.

pairs.label: The team that ran the safety evaluation also signs off on its result
pairs.detail: No function should self-approve every claim it created.

pairs.label: An irreversible, high-harm feature gets the same review depth as a reversible one
pairs.detail: Independence should increase with potential harm, uncertainty, and irreversibility.

pairs.label: Engineering decides on its own which regions the obligations apply to
pairs.detail: Legal interpretation belongs to risk and legal, with a recorded source and review date.

pairs.label: An approval from last year still authorizes today's expanded system
pairs.detail: Decisions and evidence expire deliberately rather than carrying forward.

variants.hint: Each practice is a shortcut past one specific accountability rule.
variants.explanation: Governance records only change behavior when independence, interpretation ownership, and expiry are enforced rather than assumed.
